# Phillips

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013)</sub>
- **Role:** schoolteacher  <sub>[v1 c15 P56](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0056), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr.  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013)</sub>

## Personality

Mr. Phillips exhibits a solemn demeanor and expects his pupils to show discipline while lacking the ability to maintain proper order in his own classroom. He tends to focus his attention on older students preparing for advanced exams while neglecting younger children, and he occasionally shows romantic or poetic gestures toward specific scholars.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c20 P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)_

## Traits

- solemn and stern with pupils  <sub>[v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044)</sub>
- unable to maintain proper discipline  <sub>[v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)</sub>
- attentive to advanced students over younger pupils  <sub>[v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>

## Abilities

- instructing in Queen's preparation and subjects like Latin  <sub>[v1 c15 P27](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0027), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>

## Goals

- preparing older scholars for Queen's entrance  <sub>[v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>

## History

Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea. During his tenure, he boarded at Eben Wright's house near the school. In class, he frequently used whipping as a punishment for infractions, such as when Sam Boulter spoke back to him, leading Sam's father to confront him directly. On Anne Shirley's first day of school, he humiliated her publicly by holding up her slate due to poor spelling, and later punished her for her temper by forcing her to stand on the platform in front of the blackboard. Mr. Phillips spent much of his instructional effort hearing Latin and preparing older students like Prissy Andrews for Queen's, while neglecting the younger children and allowing general classroom order to slide. During a Mayflower gathering with the scholars, he gathered flowers to give to Prissy Andrews while addressing her with quotes from books.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P27](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0027), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P56](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0056), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c16 P18](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0018), [v1 c20 P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)_

## Background by volume

- boarded at the home of Eben Wright while teaching in Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c15 P56](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0056)</sub>
- retained his teaching job partly due to his uncle being a school trustee  <sub>[v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>
